ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r4.claim: After addressing the Prophet, the discourse returns to the earlier denier, whose concern is perishable worldly gain rather than reward in an afterlife he rejects.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r4.anchor: رجع إلى حال الإنسان السابق ذكره المنكر البعث، وأن همه إنما هو في تحصيل حطام الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r5.claim: The majority read the verbs in direct address to the Quraysh unbelievers; kalla rebukes them for letting worldly desire overwhelm concern for the Hereafter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: بل تحبون العاجلة وتذرون بتاء الخطاب، لكفار قريش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p350/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p350/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p350/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari identifies kalla as a rebuke.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p350/r1.anchor: كلا ردع، وذكر في كتابه ما يوقف عليه فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p350/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p350/r2.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وقتادة والجحدري وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p350/r2.claim: They read both verbs in the third person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p350/r2.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد والحسن وقتادة والجحدري وابن كثير وأبو عمرو: بياء الغيبة فيهما

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p215/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p215/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p215/r1.claim: Preferring immediate life to the afterlife reflects the human disposition toward haste, shared across humanity, as also stated that the human was created in haste.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p215/r1.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {خُلِقَ الإنسان مِنْ عَجَلٍ} [الأنبياء: 37]

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p215/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p215/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p215/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the address as universal: humans were made hasty, so they love the immediate and leave the afterlife; he connects the tongue instruction to this rebuke.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p215/r2.anchor: جاء في (الكشاف) في قوله تعالى: {كَلاَّ بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ العاجلة}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p215/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p215/r3.speaker: الألوسي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p215/r3.claim: Al-Alusi connects love of the immediate and abandoning the afterlife to humans' haste, procrastination in repentance, false hope, and indulgence; the closest link is the desire to sin ahead.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p215/r3.anchor: وجاء في (روح المعاني) في هذه الآية: {كَلاَّ بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ العاجلة * وَتَذَرُونَ الآخرة}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r6.claim: The person loves the immediate life and leaves the afterlife, which accounts for his denial and turning away.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r3.claim: Other scenes of haste include the desire to sin ahead, the instruction not to hurry the tongue, and preferring immediate life to the afterlife.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r3.anchor: 1- قوله: {بَلْ يُرِيدُ الإنسان لِيَفْجُرَ أَمَامَهُ} والمعنى: أنه يؤثر العاجلة، فيقدم شهواته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r4.claim: The surah repeatedly pairs opposites or corresponding matters: Resurrection with the reproachful soul, sun with moon, deeds advanced with delayed, inward self-knowledge with outward excuses, and immediate life with afterlife.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r4.anchor: فالسورة تبدأ بالقسم بشيئين هما: يوم القيامة، والنفس اللوامة، ثم تستمر السورة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r1.claim: The surah pairs loving the immediate life with leaving the afterlife.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r1.anchor: وذكرت الحُبَّ والتَّرْكَ وذلك في قوله: {تُحِبُّونَ} و {وَتَذَرُونَ}

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r23.claim: After the address to the Prophet comes a general address; “kallā” rejects haste (or means “indeed”), “the immediate” is the world, and people leave the afterlife.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p216/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p216/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p216/r1.claim: Leaving the Hereafter connects visibly to the self-reproach that underlies the sūra, since the self blames itself for two kinds of failure.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p216/r1.anchor: متصلة بالنفس اللوامة التي بنيت عليها السورة اتصالاً ظاهراً. فالنفس اللوامة كما ذكرنا تلوم نفسها لأحد سببين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p217/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p217/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p217/r2.claim: The self also reproaches itself for postponing a duty until its good is lost; here the person hastens one matter and abandons another.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p217/r2.anchor: وإما أن تؤخر عملاً كان ينبغي لها عمله فيفوتها خيره، فتندم عليه، فتلوم نفسها على ذلك وهذا ما يفيده قوله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p217/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p217/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p217/r3.claim: Regret and self-reproach arise from both haste and omission, multiplying the grounds for blame.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p217/r3.anchor: فهو هنا عجّل أمراً وترك آخر فندم من الجهتين ولام نفسه في الحالتين، لام نفسه في العجلة ولام نفسه في الترك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p217/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p217/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p217/r4.claim: تذرون is preferred to تتركون because its original form توذرون loses wāw, suiting the sūra’s hurried tone.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p217/r4.anchor: ذلك أن في (تذرون) حذفاً وأصله (تَوذَرون) من (وَذِرَ) ليدل ذلك على طابع العجلة الذي يريد أن ينتهي من الشيء في أقرب وقت

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p217/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p217/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p217/r5.claim: وذر generally carries blame: وذرة is glossed as foul-smelling like meat, يا ابن شامة الوذر is an insult for slander, and a hadith calls some women الوذرة المذرة.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p217/r5.anchor: أن الفعل (وذر) في عموم معانيه يفيد الذم، ومنه قولهم: امرأة وذِرة أي: رائحها رائحة الوذْر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p218/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p218/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p218/r1.claim: ودع can denote ease, comfortable living, or calm, and رجل وديع is a quiet, settled man; the blameful context shapes the choice between the verbs.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p218/r1.anchor: الموقف موقف ذم فإنهم يحبون العاجلة ويذرون الآخرة، فاختار الفعل الذي يقال في عموم معانيه للمدح

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p218/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p218/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p218/r2.claim: People end in two groups: those who prefer and work for the Hereafter and those who love the immediate life and abandon it; this fulfills the sūra’s opening oath.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p218/r2.anchor: هذان الصنفان هما ما يؤول إلى أحدهما الناس يوم القيامة. الذي يؤثر الآخرة ويعمل لها، والذي يحب العاجلة ويذر الآخرة

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p345#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p345#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p345#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read both verbs with tāʾ, directly addressing the audience; the other readers have yāʾ in both.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p345#2/r1.anchor: قال: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو: بل تحبون [القيامة/ 20]، وتذرون [القيامة/ 21] بالتاء جميعا، وقرأ الباقون

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p345#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p345#2/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p345#2/r2.claim: The yāʾ refers back to generic al-insān, not one person, as in 70:19 followed by the exception in 70:22; the tāʾ reading means tell them that they love and leave.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p345#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: الياء على ما تقدم من ذكر الإنسان، والمراد به الكثرة، والياء حسن لتقدم الذكر

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p357#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p357#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p357#2/r1.claim: With yāʾ, the verbs return to ينبأ الإنسان, understood to mean people.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p357#2/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن قرأهما بالياء انه ردهما على معنى

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p357#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p357#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p357#2/r2.claim: With tāʾ, Muhammad is told to address them: you love the present life and leave the Hereafter.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p357#2/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن قرأهما بالتاء انه اراد قل لهم يا محمد بل تحبون العاجلة وتذرون الآخرة

QIRAAT-ER:75:21:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:75:21:2#1/r1.speaker: Imp
QIRAAT-ER:75:21:2#1/r1.claim: The Imp variant changes imperfect prefix ta- to ya-, shifting from direct plural address to third-person report while retaining root w-dh-r and object al-ākhirata.
QIRAAT-ER:75:21:2#1/r1.anchor: The variant changes the imperfect prefix from ta- to ya-, shifting from direct second-person plural address to third-person plural report

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r1.claim: Kallā guides the Messenger away from haste and urges him to wait patiently; God emphasizes this out of love for him.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r1.anchor: كلا إرشاد لرسوله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وأخذ به عن عادة العجلة وترغيب له عليه الصلاة والسلام في الأناة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r2.claim: The address generalizes to all people: humanity is hasty by nature, loves the immediate life, and abandons the afterlife; even the Prophet should not be driven by human impulse.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r2.anchor: تعميم الخطاب للكل كأنه قيل بل أنتم يا بني آدم لماخلقتم من عجل وجبلتم عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r3.claim: The explicit charge of loving the immediate life develops the earlier hint in 75:5; 75:16–19 intervenes before the direct statement, forming a progression and intensifying the reproach.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r3.anchor: ومنه يعلم أن هذا متصل بقوله سبحانه ( بل يريد الأنسان ليفجر أمامه ) فإنه ملوح

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r4.claim: The insertion also heightens the rebuke: if haste is disallowed in receiving the Qurʾān, which is healing and mercy, it is even less fitting in pursuit of what leads to depravity and ruin.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r4.anchor: وأنه إذا لم تجز العجلة في القرآن وهو شفاء ورحمة فكيف فيما هو فجور وثبور

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r5.claim: The proverb about reproaching a hide only when it has a sound surface underscores the force of reproaching those whose worldly love makes admonition ineffective.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r6.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ومجاهد والحسن وقتادة والجحدري
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and al-Jaḥdarī read both verbs in the third person; al-Ālūsī regards this as more eloquent because it gently turns the Prophet out of direct reproach.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ومجاهد والحسن وقتادة والجحدري يحبون ويذرون بباءالغيبة فيهما

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r7.claim: The second-person reading includes the addressed listener and uses a contrasting shift in address; its rhetorical effect is the reverse of the third-person reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r7.anchor: وأما القراءة بالتاء ففيها تغليب المخاطب والالتفات وهو عكس الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the claim by some heretics and early extremist Rāfiḍīs that the intervening prohibition on moving the tongue is irrelevant and proves the Qurʾān was altered; he says scholars have answered such claims.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#5/r8.anchor: وللعلماء حماة المسلمين وشهب سماء الدين في دفع كلام كثير منه ما تقدم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r1.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r1.claim: Al-Ṭībī connects kallā bal tuḥibbūn to 75:15: it rejects the person’s excuses because he persisted in sin expecting no resurrection or judgment, out of love for this life.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r1.anchor: وقال الطيب بأن قوله تعالى كلا بل تحبون العاجلة متصل بقوله تعالى ولو ألقى معاذيره

ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r7.claim: After rebuking love of the immediate life and neglect of the afterlife, the passage reinforces the warning by turning to death and the good or evil outcome of those preferences.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r7.anchor: ولما ردع سبحانه عن حب العاجلة وترك الآخرة عقب ذلك بما يتضمن تأكيد هذا الردع مما يصير إلى حسن عاقبة حب الآخرة وسوء مغبة العاجلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:21-24/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:21-24/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:21-24/r1.claim: The address shifts to the plural to generalize the rebuke and show that human beings are naturally hasty, although singular 'the human' denotes the species.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:21-24/r1.anchor: تعميم للخطاب إشعارا بأن بني آدم مطبوعون على الاستعجال وإن كان الخطاب للإنسان، والمراد به الجنس

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:21-24/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:21-24/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر والبصريون
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:21-24/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and the Basrans read both verbs with yāʾ, supporting the generic singular interpretation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:21-24/r2.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة ابن كثير وابن عامر والبصريين بالياء فيهما

BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r1.claim: The citation that God encompasses and counts everything supports the preceding point that deniers’ deeds are preserved.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r5.claim: The two lives are rival co-wives: loving one necessarily prompts conduct that distances a person from the other; love of a thing blinds and deafens.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r5.anchor: فإن الآخرة والأولى ضرتان من أحب إحداهما فعل ولا بد ما يباعده عن الأخرى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r7.claim: They abandon the Hereafter because they hate it, having committed acts that will harm them there.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r7.anchor: لانهم يبغضونها لارتكابهم ما يضربهم فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r8.claim: The plural address follows the collective meaning of human, showing that only isolated people protected by God escape blameworthy haste.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r8.anchor: وجمع الضمير وإن كان مبنى الخطاب مع الإنسان نظرا نظرا للمعنى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r9.claim: The verses use iḥtibāk: love of the present implies hatred of the Hereafter, while leaving the Hereafter implies turning toward and taking the present.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r9.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : ذكر الحب أولا دليلا على البغض ثانيا , والترك ثانيا دليلا على الإقبال والأخذ أولا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r10.claim: Unlike their souls, the Prophet’s reproaching soul urges ever more good and prompt obedience; theirs incites attachment to fleeting worldly life and abandonment of what lasts.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p251/r10.anchor: كما أن نفسك تحثك على الازدياد من الخبر والمبادرة إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p351/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p351/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p351/r1.claim: The rebuttal cancels their excuses: they prefer worldly desires and abandon the Hereafter. This combination is blameworthy; enjoying worldly life while obeying revelation is not (28:77).
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p351/r1.anchor: أي لا معاذير لهم في نفس الأمر ولكنهم أحبوا العاجلة ، أي شهوات الدنيا وتركوا الآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p351/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p351/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p351/r2.claim: Alternatively, the clause begins a new resumption that invalidates the excuses mentioned in 75:15; their excuses are false because they love the present life and neglect the next.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p351/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون إبطالا لما تضمنه قوله : { ولو ألقى معاذيره } ( القيامة : 15 ) فهو استئناف ابتدائي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p351/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p351/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p351/r3.claim: The majority read both verbs with second-person tāʾ, shifting from absent to direct address to admonish the polytheists more forcefully.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p351/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { تحبون } و { تذرون } بتاء فوقية على الالتفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p351/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p351/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p351/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Abu Amr, and Yaqub read with yāʾ, continuing the preceding third-person pronouns; the referent is the collective people meant by “the human” in 75:14.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p351/r4.anchor: وقرأه ابن كثير وابن عامر وأبو عمرو ويعقوب بياء تحتية على نسق ضمائر الغيبة السابقة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422#3/r1.claim: Continuing the preceding reading, Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr use third-person yāʾ in both verbs; the remaining readers use second-person tāʾ in both.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422#3/r1.anchor: ويذرون بالياء فيهما وقرأ الباقون بالتاء فيهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422#3/r2.claim: The people meant are the Meccan disbelievers: they love and work for this world, leaving the Hereafter by preferring worldly life over it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422#3/r2.anchor: والمراد كفار مكة يحبونها ويعملون لها ويذرون الآخرة أي يتركون العمل لها إيثارا للدنيا عليها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#12/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#12/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#12/r1.claim: They abandon the afterlife, its abode and delights, and do not work for it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#12/r1.anchor: الدار الآخرة ونعيمها فلا تعملون لها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#12/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#12/r2.speaker: مدني وكوفي
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#12/r2.claim: Medinese and Kufan readers use tāʾ in the verbs of both verses.

BURSEVI:v10p193/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p193/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p193/r5.claim: They leave the afterlife by doing no work for it and denying it.

BURSEVI:v10p193/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p193/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p193/r6.claim: The inward reading contrasts love of worldly sensual pleasure with neglect of the afterlife’s blessing of obscurity.
BURSEVI:v10p193/r6.anchor: تحبون نعمة شهوة الدنيا وتذرون نعمة خمول الآخرة والخطاب للأمة

BURSEVI:v10p195#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p195#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p195#2/r13.claim: Kallā rebukes preferring the present world to the afterlife and calls people to heed death, which ends their tie to worldly immediacy.
BURSEVI:v10p195#2/r13.anchor: ردع عن إيثار العاجلة على الآخرة أي ارتدعوا عن ذلك وتنبهوا لما بين أيديكم من الموت

QASHANI:75:20-25/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:75:20-25/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:75:20-25/r2.claim: The addressee shares with other people the human condition and natural tendency of the restless soul to love immediate life.
QASHANI:75:20-25/r2.anchor: سواء حالك وحالهم بحكم البشرية ومقتضى الطبيعة والنفس الطياشة

STUDYQURAN:75:20/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:20/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:75:20/r1.claim: The address shifts from singular, addressing the Prophet, to plural, addressing humanity in general.
STUDYQURAN:75:20/r1.anchor: These verses transition from the second-person singular, in which the Prophet is addressed, to the second-person plural, addressing humanity in general.

STUDYQURAN:75:20/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:20/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:75:20/r2.anchor: An almost identical verse is 76:27; see 76:27c.

STUDYQURAN:75:20/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:20/r3.speaker: some other schools of recitation
STUDYQURAN:75:20/r3.claim: Some recitation schools read the verbs in the third person plural: they love the ephemeral and forsake the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:75:20/r3.anchor: According to some other schools of recitation, they can be read in the third person plural

TAB-FULL:v23p505/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p505/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p505/r1.claim: People prefer the immediate world's pleasures over the later life's reward, believing in the present and denying the future.
TAB-FULL:v23p505/r1.anchor: لكن الذي دعاكم إلى قيل ذلك محبتكم الدنيا العاجلة

TAB-FULL:v23p505/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p505/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p505/r2.claim: Qatāda says most people choose the present life, except those whom God has mercy on and protects.
TAB-FULL:v23p505/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {كلا بل تحبون العاجلة وتذرون الآخرة}

SULAMI:v2p362/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p362/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p362/r1.claim: Junayd says whoever loves, pursues, and turns toward this world should expect to lose his share of the hereafter, since loving the world means abandoning the hereafter.
SULAMI:v2p362/r1.anchor: سمعت الجنيد رحمة الله عليه يقول : من احب الدنيا واقبل عليها وطلبها فليتيقن بفوت حظه من الآخرة

TABATABAI:75:20-24/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:20-24/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:20-24/r2.claim: The immediate life is worldly life; they love it and abandon the life to come.
TABATABAI:75:20-24/r2.anchor: { بل تحبون العاجلة } - أي الحياة العاجلة وهي الحياة الدنيا -

TABATABAI:75:20-24/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:20-24/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:20-24/r3.claim: The shift rejects the assumption that resurrection will not happen and replaces it with the real explanation, paralleling the shift in 75:5.
TABATABAI:75:20-24/r3.anchor: نظير الإضراب في قوله { بل يريد الإنسان ليفجر أمامه }

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r3.claim: The disbelievers of Mecca love and work for worldly life, abandoning work for the next life and preferring the former.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r3.anchor: (يعني كفار مكة يحبون الدنيا ويعملون بها ويذرون العمل للآخرة فيؤثرون الدنيا عليها.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses the afterlife here as Paradise.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r4.anchor: ونحو هذا قال الكلبي قال: (وتذرون الآخرة) أي الجنة (¬3) (¬4).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r5.claim: Both second-person ta and third-person ya readings are reported for the two verbs.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r6.claim: Al-Farra explains that the Qur’an shifts between addressing its audience and speaking of them in the third person, as in the ship passage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r6.anchor: قال الفراء: والقرآن يأتي على أن يخاطب المنزل عليهم أحيانا، وحينا يجعلون كالغيب، كقوله: {حتى إذا كنتم في الفلك وجرين بهم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r7.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r7.claim: Abu ʿAli says ya refers back to generic humanity, not one person, as in the anxious-man passage; ta means “Tell them: you love and leave.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r7.anchor: وقال أبو علي: الياء على ما تقدم من ذكر الإنسان. والمراد بالإنسان الكثرة، وليس المراد به واحدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r8.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r8.claim: Abu ʿAli explains the ta reading as an implied command to tell them that they love and leave.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p502/r8.anchor: والتاء على: قل لهم: بل تحبون وتذرون

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:20/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:20/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:20/r1.claim: After brief direct addresses to the Prophet about receiving revelation, the passage returns to humanity generally and rejects denials of resurrection, rooted in attachment to worldly pleasure and rejection of the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:20/r1.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in vahyi alışıyla ilgili özel olarak kendisine hitap eden ara cümlelerden sonra bu âyetlerde insanlığa yönelik genel bir hitapla tekrar başa dönülerek müşriklerin öldükten sonra dirilme olmayacağına dair iddiaları reddedilmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:20/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:20/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:20/r2.claim: People are censured not for loving worldly blessings themselves, which were created for them, but for abandoning the afterlife because of that love.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:20/r2.anchor: İnsanların kınanmasının sebebi dünya nimetlerini sevmeleri değil, bu yüzden âhireti terketmeleridir. Çünkü dünya nimetleri insanlar için yaratılmıştır

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r8.claim: The address ‘you love the immediate’ is to people generally, not a continuation of the Prophet’s addressee; the parenthetical instruction is unrelated to verses on either side.
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r8.anchor: قوله تعالى { كلا بل تحبون العاجلة وتذرون الآخرة } خطاب للناس وليس من تعميم الخطاب السابق في شيء لأن خطاب { لا تحرك } اعتراضي غير مرتبط بشيء من طرفيه

TABATABAI:75:36-39/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r13.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r13.claim: Al-Qummī explains tadharūna al-ākhirah as abandoning the hereafter.
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r13.anchor: { وتذرون الآخرة } قال تدعون { وجوه يومئذ ناضرة }

THALABI:v10p86#2/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p86#2/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p86#2/r15.claim: Medinan and Kufan readers use second-person plural; the other readers use third person.
THALABI:v10p86#2/r15.anchor: قرأهما أهل المدينة والكوفة بالتاء وغيرهم بالياء

THALABI:v10p86#2/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p86#2/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p86#2/r16.claim: The phrase means preferring this world to the afterlife and parallels the statement in Surat al-Insan.
THALABI:v10p86#2/r16.anchor: أي يختارون الدنيا على العقبى نظيرها في سورة الإنسان إن هؤلاء يحبون العاجلة

FARRA:v3p211/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p211/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
FARRA:v3p211/r4.claim: Ali is reported to read both verbs in second person, تحبون and تذرون; many readers have third-person يحبون.
FARRA:v3p211/r4.anchor: رويت عن علي بن أبي طالب، رحمه الله: «بل تحبون، وتذرون» بالتاء، وقرأها كثير

FARRA:v3p211/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p211/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p211/r5.claim: The Quran shifts between addressing its audience and speaking of them as absent, as in 10:22.
FARRA:v3p211/r5.anchor: والقرآن يأتي على أن يخاطب المنزل عليهم أحيانا، وحينا يجعلون كالغيب

NAHHAS:v5p83/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p83/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p83/r7.claim: He gives a short explanatory note on the following verse, saying it is later than the first.

ASAD-NOTES:75:16/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:16/r5.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:16/r5.claim: Most people love fleeting life and give no thought to the hereafter and Judgment Day.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r1.claim: The deniers have no basis for rejecting Judgment Day; their excuses arise from worldly attachment against conscience and indifference to the certain Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r1.anchor: no basis for this denial. Whatever baseless excuses they are offering originate from their love of this world

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r4.claim: After the aside about patience during piecemeal revelation, the discourse returns to its original sequence and addresses the deniers of Judgement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r4.anchor: the discourse returns to its original sequence.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r5.claim: The deniers are not short of evidence: conscience gives the strongest testimony to Judgement; they deny because they are captivated by worldly luxuries and unwilling to forgo present pleasure for the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r5.anchor: its greatest argument is found in their own conscience.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r4.speaker: أهل المدينة والكوفة، والآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r4.claim: Medinan and Kufan readers use second-person plural; the others use third-person plural. Both convey preferring and working for worldly life over the afterlife; the second-person reading addresses them directly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r4.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة والكوفة "تحبون وتذرون" بالتاء فيهما، وقرأ الآخرون بالياء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p279/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p279/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p279/r4.claim: People deny the Day of Resurrection and oppose God’s revelation and Quran because they care only for the immediate world and remain heedless of the Hereafter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p279/r4.anchor: إنما همتهم إلى الدار الدنيا العاجلة، وهم لاهون متشاغلون عن الآخرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p662#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p662#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p662#2/r11.claim: A reading uses third-person plural يحبون, which the author calls more emphatic.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p662#2/r11.anchor: وقرىء بالياء وهو أبلغ فإن قلت

MUQATIL:75:19-21/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:19-21/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:19-21/r3.claim: The Meccan unbelievers love worldly life and choose it over the afterlife, which they do not seek.
MUQATIL:75:19-21/r3.anchor: { تحبون العاجلة } [آية: 20] يعني كفار مكة، تحبون الدنيا { وتذرون } عمل { الآخرة } [آية: 21] يقول: تختارون الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة، فلا تطلبونها

MUQATIL:75:19-21/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:19-21/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:19-21/r4.claim: Muqatil points to a corresponding warning in the opening phrase of al-Insan.
MUQATIL:75:19-21/r4.anchor: نظيرها في { هل أتى على الإنسان } { تحبون العاجلة وتذرون الآخرة } [القيامة: 20، 21]

QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r14.claim: Qurtubi identifies the addressees as Meccan unbelievers, al-ʿājila as this world and its life, and leaving the hereafter as abandoning its deeds.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r15.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r15.claim: Some exegesis identifies the hereafter here specifically as Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r15.anchor: وفي بعض التفسير قال: الآخرة الجنة

QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r16.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r16.claim: Medinese and Kufan readers use second-person forms; Abu Ubayd selects this direct address despite the alternative.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r16.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة والكوفيون «بل تحبون» «وتذرون» بالتاء فيهما على الخطاب واختاره أبو عبيد

QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r17.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r17.claim: Other readers use third-person forms; Abu Hatim prefers them as a return to al-insān, understood collectively as people.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r17.anchor: الباقون بالياء على الخبر، وهو اختيار أبي حاتم، فمن قرأ بالياء

QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r18.claim: The second-person reading confronts the unbelievers with blame, making the point more forceful.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r18.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتاء فعلى أنه واجههم بالتقريع لأن ذلك أبلغ في المقصود

QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21#2/r1.claim: Qurtubi supports this description of people loving the immediate life and leaving the hereafter with a parallel in Sūrat al-Insān.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21#2/r1.anchor: إن هؤلاء يحبون العاجلة ويذرون ورآءهم يوما ثقيلا
